## M7 — The slow tick

**M7.A.1** `basic_level` **MUST NOT** be advanced by any move or by any per-exchange increment. It **MUST** be recomputed on the slow tick as the estimator of M1.A.4a–M1.A.4c over `functional_level` history. Recovery of `functional_level` toward baseline when calm **MUST NOT** be a symmetric restoring force.

**M7.A.1a** — *the dependence gate **MUST** run on the slow clock too.* `M1.A.15`'s `financially_dependent` flag currently gates one **move** (M5.C). `FE04.9` puts the same condition on **basic-level change itself**: change requires that the person be **self-sustainingly independent of the family of origin**. Therefore `basic_level` **MUST NOT** rise on the slow tick while the agent is financially dependent, however many exchanges completed. Without this gate an agent accumulates `functional_level` gains and ratchets `basic_level` upward while still inside the exact condition under which the change-back reaction's third rung has teeth (M1.A.15) — which would make M5.C's fast-clock gate cosmetic. → *decision B1-tail, 2026-08-27*; `theory/family_evaluation/fe04.md` · FE04.9

**M7.A.2** — *amended.* Differentiation gained in a peripheral system **MUST NOT** transfer automatically to the nuclear family. **The capacity transfers; the application is re-earned per tie.** `basic_level` is per-person and rises on the M1.A.4a estimator; **applying** it in a given relationship requires observing the reciprocity **in that relationship**. → §10, §15 Ch10/Ch21; `kerr_book/ks16.md` · KS16.9
**The evidence is unambiguous.** Kerr had been "**teaching this cocreation idea to students of Bowen theory for over twenty-five years**" before observing it in his own marriage (`ks16.md` · KS16.6); and Mr. S. held systems thinking for his sister's triangle, his sons' triangle and his family history while lacking it in his marriage — "**I acknowledge Bowen theory, but I don't feel it**" (`ks17.md` · KS17.1).

**M7.A.2a** — *resolved, 2026-08-25.* `systems_perspective` is a **per-person state with per-tie attenuation by load** (M1.A.18d), not a per-tie state variable. The "application re-earned per tie" in M7.A.2 is therefore **not** a second acquisition — it is the same capacity reaching a tie whose intensity had previously exceeded it. No new state; the attenuation term does the work.

**M7.A.2b** The **family of origin is the privileged peripheral system**, not any peripheral system — it is the highest-load context (`ks06.md` · KS06.8) so gains demonstrated there carry the most evidential weight, and it is where the assumptions being tested were formed. Where the parents are dead, ties to **anyone who carried the same triangle** substitute — "much can be gained by working on relationships with people who were close to the parents, such as aunts and uncles." → `ks13.md` · KS13.11

**M7.B.1** `chronic_anxiety` **MUST** be fixed once in childhood from witnessed history (M1.A.7). The age is `[I]`. After that it **MUST** change only when `basic_level` rises, falling with the rise; it **MUST NOT** drift otherwise, and **MUST NOT** rise when `basic_level` falls (the owner: "chronic anxiety stays fixed unless level of differentiation goes up, thus it's fixed for some time"). This supersedes `M1.A.7a`'s per-slow-tick derivation for everyone past the fixation age; `M1.A.7a`'s three terms set the value fixed in childhood for people born in the run.

**M7.B.1a** — *chronic anxiety before the fixation age.* For a person younger than the fixation age (12, `M2.A.0a`), chronic anxiety **MUST** be derived each slow tick: the mean of their parents' chronic anxiety (the field), plus `witnessed_gain` (0.5, `[I]`) times the child's mean load over the year, acute anxiety above the chronic floor (their own witnessed history, `M1.A.7`; the load above their *usual* level averages to about zero by construction, so it cannot be the reading). It is read each slow tick through the one on which the child turns 12, so the year lived at 11 counts. Only living parents are read; an orphan keeps the value they have. At the fixation age it **MUST** be fixed, and `M7.B.1` governs from then on. A child present at `t0` starts from the parents' mean. This is `M1.A.7a`'s derivation for the people `M2.A.0a` names, made concrete. The owner (2026-10-13): "chronic Anxiety builds over childhood." The load term **MUST** be the mean of the child's yearly mean loads over every year of childhood observed in the run, through the year lived at 11, not that year alone. The years observed start at birth, or at `t0` for a child present then.

**M7.C.1** Life stage **MUST** govern childhood, launch, partnering and mortality.

**M7.C.1a** — *the addition of a tie **MUST** be modelled as a **redistribution of a conserved investment budget**, not as a stressor.* A new claimant reduces every existing tie's share **by construction**; nothing bad need happen. This is M1.A.10's zero-sum allocation operating **between ties**. → `kerr_book/ks22.md` · KS22.2
Two instances with different claimant types — a child (KS22.2) and a fiancée (`ks25.md` · KS25.5) — so the mechanism is the **redistribution**, not the kind of tie.

**M7.C.1b** The redistribution **MUST** be able to move **`investment` and `expectations` in opposite directions on one tie simultaneously** — her investment fell while her expectations of him rose. A scalar tie state cannot express this; `M4.C.1`'s four signed channels (M1.A.9a, KS10.1) can. → `ks22.md` · KS22.2

**M7.C.1c** The **effect** of the redistribution **MUST** scale with the affected tie's **share of the agent's total investment**, not with the event. Same nodal event type, same person, six years apart, opposite outcomes: a low-investment partner's pregnancy produced no episode; a high-investment partner's preceded the breakdown. "**John not committing fully to either relationship distanced him from their dependence on him and also his dependence on them.**" → `ks22.md` · KS22.3

**M7.C.1d** — *withdrawal at extreme fusion is a **removal**, not a differentiation.* Where a person's fusion is concentrated in a **single** tie with no alternatives, a reduction in the supporting party's investment **MUST** be resolved as a removal event (`M11.C.11`), **not** as a differentiating move — regardless of the withdrawing party's intent. The two are distinguishable **only** by the other's remaining alternative ties. → `ks25.md` · KS25.3, KS25.4; `ks21.md` · KS21.9
**Two independent cases, forty-three years apart.** Bowen, the morning after: "**Mike, I think your mother pulled up and Billy suicided.**" And Nancy Lanza's withdrawal had the *form* of the move — reducing overfunctioning, redirecting energy to her own life, explicitly hoping it would produce independence — with **none** of the preconditions in `kerr_book/ks15.md` · KS15.1. **This is the model's most consequential asymmetry and MUST NOT be softened.**

**M7.C.1e** Mortality (`M7.C.1`) **MUST** remove a Person only through `M6.3`'s named mechanism. → `model_explainer.md` §18 · C15

**M7.C.1f** — *who acts.* The owner (2026-10-13): a person "starts acting at 10, stops acting at death". A person **MUST** select moves (`M3.E.1`'s activation) only from `acting_age` (10) until death. A younger child **MUST** still perceive, appraise, carry anxiety and symptom load, and witness. Every family member who acts **MUST** carry an age, advanced on the slow tick; a partner's family-of-origin holder, who never acts, carries none.

**M7.C.1g** — *launch.* At `launch_age` (20, `[I]`; the age `M7.E.1f`'s development levels off) a child **MUST** leave the parental household for a household of their own, and **MUST** become an earner and not financially dependent. Their ties stay. The owner approved 20 in the review of 2026-10-16.

**M7.C.1h** — *partners come from settings.* The owner (2026-10-13): "Provide settings for partners." Partners **MUST** be declared in config, never invented by the engine: one row per partner, naming the member they partner, that member's age at pairing, the partner's age gap, sex, chronic anxiety, sibling rank and sibship size, channel prior, and a family-of-origin holder (`M1.D.8`, in `M2.3`'s bond-energy-only form). At pairing the partner **MUST** enter as a new person. Their basic level **MUST** be drawn within `M2.A.0e`'s ±1 of the member's level at that moment, from the run's draw stream, so the pairing rule holds by construction. The couple **MUST** form a new household and a new `Family` (`M1.D.1`), whose budget is `budget_per_undifferentiation × (100 − the couple's mean basic level)` (`[I]`; 1.49 gives about 90, the `ravi_marta` family's budget). The spouse tie **MUST** be added as a redistribution of the member's investment (`M7.C.1a`). *Not built in D-II:* `M2.A.0f`'s pairs that fail to form.

**M7.C.1i** — *births come from the same settings.* Each partner row **MUST** declare the couple's children: how many, and the years after pairing at which each is born. A birth **MUST** create a person whose identifier derives from the parents' identifiers and birth order (`M1.A.20`), at age 0, with sex and channel prior declared in the row or drawn from the run's stream. Their basic level is the parents' mean (`M7.E.1f`), their chronic anxiety comes from `M7.B.1a`, and parent and sibling ties start at declared values. `M7.E.1c`'s five situations are evaluated at the birth.

**M7.C.1j** — *mortality.* Each family member's age at death **MUST** be drawn once, from the run's stream, when they enter the run (at `t0`, conditioned on being alive at their starting age; at birth or partnering otherwise), from a declared hazard by age, `hazard(a) = mortality_a × exp(mortality_b × a)` (`[I]`; a Gompertz curve whose parameters put the median age at death near 80). The death falls on the slow tick at which that age is reached. This keeps `M1.F.6`'s rule: no per-tick draw. The owner has stated no rule for when people die. An external agent does not die in the run: they retire (`M2.A.0k`).

**M7.C.1k** — *`FIND_WORK`, a goal-directed act of the life course, not a move.* It is not in `M5`'s repertoire: it has no target, and the relationship policy (`M4.D`) does not select it. It is open only to a living, acting member of a household with an unresolved loss of income (`M6.3h`) who is at least `working_age_years` (16, `[I]`), and it always succeeds (the owner: "Trying equals finding"). Each week each such member takes it with probability `find_work_rate × min(1, load above their usual level ÷ find_work_pressure_scale)` (`[I]`), drawn from the run's stream: who takes it, and when, **MUST** follow from the members' own state, the pressure the loss puts on each, and **MUST NOT** be scheduled. It is logged as a life event that reaches the household.

**M7.C.1l** — *an addition or transition carries a load.* (The owner, 2026-10-19, E2 of `docs/PROPOSAL — EVENT SIZES FROM THE HOLMES–RAHE SCALE.md`: an owner decision, `[I]`, with no source cited for it; the correction of 2026-10-19 to that proposal's §2 stands beside it.) Each of `PARTNERING` (`M7.C.1h`), `BIRTH` (`M7.C.1i`), launch (`M7.C.1g`), the coach's retirement (`M2.A.0k`) and `FIND_WORK` (`M7.C.1k`) **MUST** also raise a lasting stressor sized by `M1.F.6a` (`PARTNERING_LOAD` 50 LCU to each partner; `BIRTH_LOAD` 39 to the parents and the child's siblings; `LAUNCH_LOAD` 29 to the child and the parents still in their household; `RETIREMENT_LOAD` 45 to the coachee at reach the coach tie's `bond_energy ÷ 100`; `FIND_WORK_LOAD` 26 to the household), each weighing for the table's 12 weeks (the owner). The life event itself stays what it was (`M4.A.2`'s nodal reach for the nodal ones); the load is an exogenous stressor, counted as one (`M1.F.7`). No rule reads an outcome from the load (`M10.C.5`). → `M1.F.6a`

**M7.D.1** Symptom load **MUST** accumulate from routed load and, on crossing threshold, **MUST** emit an **endogenous** event (M1.F.7). Built in Phase C, because `M4.C.3`'s integrator is and six Phase C criteria read time to threshold. Every channel is checked for onset each week, not only the one being fed: load left in a channel can cross when functional level falls, and each crossing is its own onset event.

**M7.D.1a** — *a symptom's own load.* (The owner, 2026-10-19, E3 of `docs/PROPOSAL — EVENT SIZES FROM THE HOLMES–RAHE SCALE.md`.) At an onset (`M7.D.1`) the bearer **MUST** receive a lasting stressor `OWN_ILLNESS` (53 LCU at reach 1, `M1.F.6a`) and each living family member on an interactive tie to them `FAMILY_ILLNESS` (44 LCU at reach `bond_energy ÷ 100`; an external agent on such a tie, the coach, takes none, as `M7.D.2a`'s release passes them by, `M1.E.7e`), each for the table's 12 weeks. They arrive the week after the onset (`RunState.arising`, injected at step 2; a load that misses its week raises), since an exogenous stressor has no latency and the onset is read in step 9. They carry the stressor mechanism (`exogenous=True`, as `M1.F.7` requires of it) on the `ENDOGENOUS` channel, because their cause is an event of the run: the evaluation readout's stress term (`M11.G.2`) leaves them out, so a family's own symptoms do not count as stress from outside. → `M1.F.6a`, `M7.D.2a`

**M7.D.2** The three channels **MUST** be substitutable — the same deficit **MUST** be able to present as any of the three. The load goes to the expressed channel (`M1.A.11c`); every channel leaks.

**M7.D.2a** — *symptom **lock-in**.* Once a member is carrying symptom load, the **family's subsequent anxiety MUST fall**, producing a stable configuration that **resists the symptom's removal**. → `kerr_book/ks23.md` · KS23.1 Each person holds `symptom_bound`, the anxiety the family's focus on their active symptom holds (a stock in `M6.4`). Each week, for a bearer whose most loaded active channel has severity `x` (load ÷ threshold), `s(x) = lock_in_gain × x × (1 − x / lock_in_turn)` (0.2 and 3, `[I]`). While `s > 0`, each partner on an interactive tie moves `s ×` their excess above usual into the bearer's hold: the family calms around the symptom. When the symptom ends (re-arm), or a `binder_unavailable` names its channel (`M1.F.9`), the whole hold goes back to the partners on interactive ties, split by bond energy among the bearer's interactive ties to living members (G2, `docs/PROPOSAL — RELEASE BY TIE (G2).md`: an external agent, `M1.A.17`, takes none; with every such tie at zero bond energy the split is equal; with no such tie the hold stays with the bearer), and that is the release `M11.C.12` reads. Removal (`INSTITUTIONALIZE`) makes the ties non-interactive, so the hold neither fills nor empties; the bearer keeps it. No rule writes resistance to removal or relief on it. *Not built:* the hold does not feed the bearer's integrator, so lock-in does not by itself make a symptom chronic.
**This one requirement yields three observed behaviours as consequences**, none of which the spec previously produced: **chronicity** without any pathology; **relapse on cure** (`M11.C.12`); and **relief on removal** of the symptomatic member (`ks20.md` · KS20.8 — "the family tensions dropped significantly during Gary's time in reform school"). It is also why the Nash marriage stabilised around the deteriorating son (`ks22.md` · KS22.13).

**M7.D.2b** Removal of a member **MUST** produce **opposite-signed** effects on different members, keyed to their position relative to the removed one — not a uniform family-level shift. When Gary Gilmore was removed the family relaxed and **only his mother** wanted him back; when both of Nash's son's parents died, **the projection target improved**. → `ks20.md` · KS20.8; `ks22.md` · KS22.8

**M7.D.2c** — *the three channels are **mutually protective**, not merely substitutable.* M7.D.2 makes them alternatives for the same deficit. The source goes further: **occupancy of one channel lowers the hazard on the others** — reciprocal functioning **within** a single person, the same shape M1.B.6 gives a dyad. Therefore symptom hazard in each channel **MUST** be reduced by load already carried in another, and a model that treats the three as independent draws is a failing implementation. Consequence: **a person carrying one symptom is protected against a second**, which is what makes channel-switching visible as an event rather than as accumulation. → `theory/family_evaluation/fe01.md` · FE01.6, `fe05.md` · FE05.8 What enters a channel each week is divided by `1 + channel_protection × Σ (load in the other channels) / threshold` (`channel_protection` 1.0, `[I]`).

**M7.D.2d** — *lock-in **MUST** be non-monotone in severity, and this **amends** M7.D.2a.* M7.D.2a as written makes the stabilising effect grow without limit, so a severe enough symptom becomes maximally stabilising. Three independent statements say the curve turns over: past a severity threshold the symptom **destabilises** the configuration it was stabilising, and removal then brings **relief** rather than the resistance M7.D.2a predicts. The stabilising term **MUST** therefore rise with symptom load to a peak and fall beyond it, and `M11.C.22` **MUST** test both limbs. This is what reconciles M7.D.2a's resistance-to-removal with M7.D.2b's relief-on-removal: they are the same curve either side of the turn. → `theory/family_evaluation/fe03.md` · FE03.9, `fe07.md` · FE07.15 Past the turn (`s < 0`), `min(1, |s|)` of the hold goes back to the partners each week, and the same share of the bearer's own excess above usual spills to them, split by bond energy as the release is (G2): the symptom no longer holds what it held, nor the bearer's own anxiety. Both are transfers in `M6.4`.

**M7.D.3** — **WITHDRAWN as a mechanism at revision 11.** It read: curing a symptom without changing the underlying deficit must raise family tension. The result is kept as `M11.C.12`'s and `M11.C.15`'s assertion, and **MUST** arise from the release of the anxiety the symptom was binding (`M6.I.1`) into ties whose learned patterns then carry it. A rule that writes the rise **MUST NOT** be implemented.

**M7.E.4** — *ties **MUST** deteriorate by default, at a rate inverse to level.* A relationship left alone does not hold its state: without active work it degrades, and it degrades **faster the lower the pair's `basic_level`**. Each tie **MUST** therefore carry a slow-clock decay on conductance and a slow-clock accrual on bond energy, scaled inversely to level, which any `STAY-IN-CONTACT` or completed exchange offsets. The decay **MUST** be driven by the two members' chronic anxiety (the owner: chronic anxiety "wears on ties, which is why the other emotional patterns act up from time to time, often triggered by other stressors"), and the bond-energy accrual is withdrawn, since `M1.B.4` holds bond energy at or near zero decay. A worn tie has less slack, so a spell pushes it past where the patterns relieve; no rule writes the flare. **This is what makes `M11.C.17`'s coach-free arm a real test rather than a trivial one**: a flat arm produced by *nothing happening* proves nothing, whereas a flat arm produced by decay and effort cancelling is a result. → `theory/family_evaluation/fe03.md` · FE03.13

**M7.D.4** Removal (`INSTITUTIONALIZE`) **MUST** fire off the **remaining members'** tolerance for disturbing behaviour, explicitly decoupled from the symptom-bearer's severity, and **MUST** be suppressible by relocating decision ownership (M5.C.1). → §6.2 Each week, if a living member has an active symptom, and another member on an interactive tie to the member carrying the most active symptom load has excess above usual greater than their `tolerance` (`M1.D.5`, declared per person; none listed, never), that member sends an endogenous `INSTITUTIONALIZE` of the bearer. It reads the others' anxiety, not the bearer's severity. A family with `decision_ownership_external` set (`M5.C.1`) never fires it. No criterion in Phase D I depends on it; it is pinned by `tests/bowen/test_symptoms.py::test_m7d4_removal_fires_off_the_others_tolerance_not_the_bearers_severity`.

**M7.E.1** The generational update **MUST** produce: the primary projection object **lower** than the parents, minimally-involved siblings about the same, those outside the process **better**. **The ordering is a result, not a rule.** It **MUST** be produced through `M1.A.4a`'s estimator reading each child's own `functional_level` history, not by writing the ordering. A child born in the run **MUST** start from a birth prior centred on the parents' level (`M2.A.0c`), `[I]` in spread; its `basic_level` at launch is what the estimator reads from its childhood. Generations 1 and 2 are not simulated through childhood (`M2.A.0a`), so for them the ordering is an initial condition. The birth prior and the age at which the estimate is taken are Phase D plan items. For a child, `M7.E.1f` replaces the estimator from 5 to 20; the estimator governs from 20, as for any adult. The owner set the ages and the band (P14); replacing the estimator with `M7.E.1f`'s rule is Claude's recommendation 2026-10-13, approved by the owner 2026-10-16.

**M7.E.1a** — *the transmission rule, stated; a shape check on the output.* With `M7.E.1` amended, the three-outcome distribution below is checked on the output in `M10.C.4`'s sense and **MUST NOT** be used to assign a child's level. Parents are at the **same** level (M2.A.0c), and "**they can produce children with basic levels a little higher, a little lower, or the same as their levels**" — a **three-outcome distribution centred on the parental level**, with the child's own parental triangle (M7.E.1b) deciding which offset. It **MUST NOT** average dissimilar parents (they are not dissimilar) and **MUST NOT** impose a guaranteed decline: the projection **line** declines, the family does not. → `kerr_book/ks11.md` · KS11.2

**M7.E.1b** — *siblings differ because they occupy **different parental triangles**, not because they received different event counts.* "**siblings grow up in the same family but in different triangles.**" The four differentiating properties are of the *triangle*: less/more anxious investment, more/less mature interactions, more goal-directed / more relationship-oriented, more/less "self". Strongest evidence in the corpus: a mother of **identical twins** describing one relationship as "**almost addicted**" to mutual reactivity and the other as markedly less so. → `ks09.md` · KS09.1

**M7.E.1c** — *five situations raise parental anxiety focused on a child; they do not select the target.* The closed list, evaluated against the family's history at each birth: **the firstborn; the firstborn of a given sex; a child born with a reality defect; a child born at a time of high stress in the family, nuclear or extended; the last-born.** More than one child may be a focus. Because the fourth is a **timing** condition, target selection is history-dependent and therefore **emergent** — which is the correct shape. → `ks09.md` · KS09.2. Each situation present at a birth **MUST** add to the parents' anxious focus on that child's tie (`M1.B.8`'s investment), `[I]` in size, and **MUST NOT** assign the target. Which child becomes the target follows from where that focus is relieved — the child whose accommodating acts calm a parent is reinforced (`M4.D.6e`) — so `M2.A.2`'s requirement that the target be an outcome is met by mechanism. A declared `weakness` is the reality defect (`M1.B.8a`), and it **MUST** act from `t0` for a child present then as well as from birth, through `M1.B.8a`'s weekly shortfall rather than as a situation here. The other four situations are not applied at `t0`, because no history before `t0` is declared to evaluate them against (accepted by the owner, plan §4.8)

**M7.E.1d** — *the projection **MUST** be able to initiate with **no signal from the child**.* It is a self-fulfilling prophecy in Merton's sense: "the process begins with **a false definition of a situation that evokes a new behavior, which makes the false conception come true**", and "**The defect may also be a total product of the mother's imagination.**" Checked against an independent record in **one** family — home movies. *Corrected 2026-08-28: the requirement said two families with home movies in both. "Home movies" occurs once in the source, for Kerr's own family, and the second family cited is the same one.*. → `ks09.md` · KS09.3; `ks25.md` · KS25.7

**M7.E.1e** Transmission **MUST** read the parents' functional level **on the marital tie**, not a global average: "**how people manage themselves in the intimate relationship with their spouses, and not how they manage themselves in their work lives, is the primary determinant of the basic levels of differentiation of their offspring.**" → `ks06.md` · KS06.8. Met through the mechanism — a child's functional history is driven by its parental triangle, which reads the marital tie — and checked on the output.

**M7.E.1f** — *a child's basic level develops from 5 to 20, within 2% of the parents'.* The owner (2026-10-13): it "starts at 5 and grows each year to level off at year 20, ± 2% of parents, depending on circumstances and how the parents are functioning. Parents functioning up boost the child's basic level, functioning down degrade it", and the band is "level × .02, not two more points". Before 5 a child's basic level **MUST** be held at the parents' mean basic level, and the estimator **MUST NOT** run. At 5 that mean **MUST** be fixed as the child's anchor `a`. Each slow tick from 5 to 20 the level **MUST** move by `development_rate × d` (`development_rate` 0.1, `[I]`), clipped to `a × (1 ± 0.02)`, where `d` is half the parents' mean `functional_level − basic_level` over the year and half the child's own (the circumstances: the child's own functioning comes from their place in the parental triangle, `M7.E.1b`, so siblings can differ without a rule assigning which). From 20 the estimator (`M1.A.4a`) governs, with `M7.A.1a`'s gate. Nothing writes the ordering `M7.E.1` asks for; `M7.E.1a`'s three outcomes stay a check on the output. The band is not a flat ±2% (the owner, 2026-10-16, after the review). "No attention +-2%"; "supportive, responsible behaviour attention - up to 5% growth"; "projection up to 10% negative" ("Projection can be the significant driver of negative pressure"). A child whose parents send them no acts ends within ±2% of the anchor; supportive acts open room to rise toward +5%, projection-type acts room to fall toward −10% (form: plan §4.11, R31.B7). Under a flat ±2%, ten generations could fall at most from 100 to about 82, so `M11.C.6`'s limit (a) could not be met; it is restated (`M11.C.6`). From 5 to 20 the acts either living parent sends the child are counted, each one, by whether it is projection-type (`OVERFUNCTION`, `PURSUE`, `TRIANGLE`, the `projection` set of `config/bowen/pattern_acts.md`) or supportive (a self-directed move, `config/bowen/event_kinds.md`). With `p` and `s` the shares of all parental acts to the child so far that were each (0 when there were none), the band is `a × (1 − 0.02 − 0.08 p)` to `a × (1 + 0.02 + 0.03 s)`, and it **MUST** only limit the year's step: a step **MUST NOT** carry the level below the floor or above the ceiling, and a band that narrows under a level (the shares change over childhood) **MUST NOT** move it; the level stays until the development rule moves it back inside (review 2026-10-16: clipping the level itself pushed it whenever a share fell). The constants are `development_band` 0.02, `development_band_projection` 0.10 and `development_band_support` 0.05, all `[I]`, the owner's values. The development rule is unchanged: the acts open room, they do not move the level. Known weakness of the share form: a child who receives few acts, all projection, gets the full −10% room.

**M7.E.2** The generational rate **MUST** be stochastic — fast for a few generations, static for one or two, then fast again — and reversible at both extremes. A fixed per-generation decrement **MUST NOT** be implemented; no such rate exists in the corpus. → §8

**M7.E.3** — **WITHDRAWN as a mechanism at revision 11.** It read: cutoff must form a positive feedback loop — more intense cutoff → more exaggerated parental problem in the next marriage → more intense cutoff in the generation after. The loop is kept as `M11.C.10`'s assertion and **MUST** arise from mechanisms the spec already has: the child witnesses cutoff (`M1.A.7`, `M1.F.5`), its automatic channel learns from it (`M4.D.6`), and the next marriage takes cutoff from the families of origin as an input to its intensity (`M1.D.8`).
